card.name: tip-height
card.title: Your TV is too high.
card.body: Eye level means the centre of the screen, sitting down.

card.name: teach-arc
card.title: One remote for TV and soundbar.
card.body: Use the HDMI port marked ARC, then switch on CEC.

card.name: tip-studs
card.title: Drywall alone will not hold it.
card.body: Studs or rated anchors. There is no third option.

card.name: tip-fireplace
card.title: It can be done right.
card.body: Mind the heat. A mantel mount brings the screen down.
fact: of fire, then feel the wall

card.name: teach-raceway
card.title: Two honest ways to hide wires.
card.body: A paintable channel takes an hour. In wall is cleaner.

card.name: teach-prep
card.title: Five minutes of prep helps.
card.body: Clear the floor at the wall and unbox the TV beforehand.
fact: of clear floor at the wall

card.name: tip-distance
card.title: How far back should you sit?
card.body: About eight and a half feet from a 65 inch. Screen size times 1.6.

card.name: teach-heat
card.title: Run the fire for ten minutes.
card.body: Put your hand where the screen would sit. Warm is fine.

card.name: tip-mounts
card.title: Pick by the room, not the price.
card.body: Fixed, tilting or full motion. Send a photo of your wall.

card.name: teach-motion
card.title: Turn off motion smoothing.
card.body: It is usually on out of the box. Look under Picture.

card.name: tip-renters
card.title: You can still mount it.
card.body: Check your lease, use proper anchors, patch when you leave.
fact: to patch on the way out

card.name: teach-wall
card.title: Knock. It tells you what it is.
card.body: Hollow is drywall. Dull is plaster. Cold and hard is concrete.
